title: Remove unused resolver and duplicate TLS features
description:
Narrow the default Rust dependency feature graph to the capabilities the product actually uses. Local JSON Schema validation must not compile remote-resolution infrastructure, and remote document access must select one TLS implementation while preserving supported HTTPS and compressed-response behavior.

## Background

The default `jsonschema` feature set pulls HTTP resolution through Reqwest, Hyper, Rustls, Tokio-Rustls, and AWS-LC even though repository schemas use local fragment references. `ureq` currently combines its default Rustls stack with an explicitly selected native-TLS backend.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The default `jsonschema` dependency disables default features, and the resolved default workspace graph contains no `reqwest`, `hyper`, `tokio-rustls`, or `aws-lc-rs` path introduced for JSON Schema resolution.
- [hard] REQ-02: The default `ureq` dependency disables default features and enables exactly one intentional TLS backend for remote document access, with any required content-decoding feature selected explicitly.
- [hard] REQ-03: `cargo tree -e features --workspace` demonstrates exactly one enabled TLS implementation on the remote-document path and no remote JSON Schema resolver feature.
- [hard] REQ-04: Existing local schema-validation behavior passes unchanged, including local fragment references to priority and state definitions.
- [hard] REQ-05: Automated tests cover successful HTTPS remote-document access and any supported compressed response behavior using the selected feature set, without depending on a second TLS backend.
- [hard] REQ-06: A deterministic dependency-feature assertion fails if remote JSON Schema resolution or an additional TLS backend returns to the default graph.
